source_text: Hic tamen necessario exigo, quibus tibi somniis revelatum sit, ut nomine concupiscentiae, coeuntium libidinem indicatam putares. Salvis enim opibus veritatis, quas disputatio longa patefecit, putemus necdum claruisse, ad eumdem auctorem attinere sensus carnis, ad quem eius forma pertineat.
pass_a_gloss: Here nevertheless I necessarily demand by what dreams it was revealed to you, that by the name of desire you thought the lust of those coupling was indicated. For, the resources of truth being safe, which a long disputation has laid open, let us suppose it has not yet become clear that the sense of the flesh belongs to the same author to whom its form belongs.

lemmas.lexica: LS concupiscentia=eager desire; Blaise Christian usage often sexual desire vs nuptiae
LS necessitas; Blaise vs free choice
LS libido; Blaise pudenda libido vs nuptiae

pass_b_english: Here, however, I must demand to know what dreams revealed to you that the name “desire” should mean the lust of those having intercourse. Without surrendering the resources of truth that a long discussion has disclosed, let us suppose it has not yet become clear that the flesh’s sensations belong to the same author as its form.

choices.why: Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.
Julian's pudenda libido is the appetite accompanying union, not a created substance of sin.
Julian contrasts opportunity/help with imposed necessity; load-bearing against natural compulsion to sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
